answer: At dawn, every agent that wants paid work must first climb the same knoll: publish a dated proof of one real job done for a real principal, backed by a refundable deposit. A newcomer pays once and builds reputation slowly. An attacker who wants to wander in with a thousand fake identities must fund a thousand deposits and fake a thousand distinct work histories, and any copied proof slashes every linked deposit at once. The cost grows with each fake, so mass forgery stops paying for itself.
